column1: # INLINE MARKERS.
# Written in a page as   [some text]{.marker}   or bare as   {.marker}
# and, where the row has a PREFIX, as a link:   [some text](@rel:table-events)
# EVERY ROW BELONGS TO A CLASS (theme/marker-classes.tsv), and the class supplies
# the default shape and colour. Read that file first -- it is where the families
# are defined and where the reasoning lives.
# ADDING ONE IS A ROW HERE. No code change, no CSS change.
# EVERY USE IS COUNTED IN THE BUILD REPORT, GROUPED BY CLASS. That is the actual
# point -- a marker nobody can list is just a colour. It is what lets you ask
# "what is unconfirmed across this whole site" and get an answer, and grouping by
# class is what keeps that answer clean now that not every marker is a confidence
# claim.
# COLUMNS
# marker   the token you type: {.tbc}
# class    which family this belongs to. REQUIRED. See marker-classes.tsv.
# label    shown when used bare, with no text of its own
# shape    OVERRIDE the class shape. Blank = inherit.
#          box - plain - strike - soft
# color    OVERRIDE the class colour. Blank = inherit -- and inheriting is the
#          better path: the class colour is a generated CSS rule, so one cell
#          repaints the whole family, where an override is inline on every span.
# prefix   the `@x:` namespace this marker answers to, giving it a LINK form.
#          Blank = span-only, which is the normal case.
# tooltip  hover text. Say what the READER should DO about it.
# THE `prefix` COLUMN -- what it buys and what it costs (2026-08-09)
# A span records a MENTION. A link records an EDGE: links.py writes source ->
# target into the reference graph for every reference it resolves, and
# docindex.py publishes it as /doc-refs.json. So `[fkCal](@rel:table-events)` puts
# a real relationship in a real graph, where `[fkCal]{.rel}` can only be counted.
# Nothing new is computed to get that -- the resolution was already happening to
# build the href. It was simply being thrown away.
# THE COLUMN IS ALSO WHY THE ENGINE COULD BE SPLIT. markers.py used to hardcode
# `_TERM_CLASS = "terminology"` and claim `@term:` itself, and argued that a
# second module would be a second place naming the family. Naming the family in a
# CELL retired that argument: both forms read the same row, so neither module
# names anything. docrender/markerlinks.py contains no marker name at all.
# COSTS, both real:
#   A namespace is claimed at IMPORT, so a prefix ADDED during a live
#   `mkdocs serve` session is not live until the process restarts. Reported.
#   A prefix here can COLLIDE with `@data:`, `@img:` or a peer site slug. All
#   three are checked and reported, and the existing owner always wins. Nothing
#   in this file can fail a build.
# WRITE THE PREFIX THE SAME AS THE MARKER unless there is a reason not to.
# `.rel` / `@rel:` is one idea with one name. `.relat` beside `@rel:` was the
# first draft and was rejected on the spot: two names for one thing is the defect
# that retired three manifests in brain-config.
# SHAPE AND COLOUR ARE SEPARATE AXES, and that split is the whole flexibility.
# There are only FOUR shapes because a reader can distinguish four at a glance
# and cannot distinguish nine. Colour is free.
#   box     bordered chip, tinted background. Demands attention.
#   plain   coloured text, no chrome. Present but not shouting.
#   strike  struck through. Superseded, kept findable.
#   soft    italic, prefixed with ~. Approximate rather than doubtful.
# FOUR HAS NOW HELD THREE TIMES RUNNING: terminology wanted colour without an
# underline (`plain`, already there); highlight wanted a heavier tint (a NUMBER on
# `box`, not a shape); and the FMP families split on `box` against `plain`. A
# BOXED LINK needed no fifth shape either -- an anchor from a `box` family wears
# `dr-mark--box` without `dr-mark`, so it gets the chip and skips the help cursor.
# PREFER INHERITING, THEN A TOKEN, AND ONLY THEN A HEX. A token follows the theme
# into light mode and into every other site; a hex is frozen where you typed it
# and will be wrong on the scheme you were not looking at.
# THE BOX SHAPE MEANS A COLOUR HAS TO SURVIVE ITS OWN BACKGROUND. `box` tints the
# chip with the class's `wash` of the marker's own colour, so the text is not
# sitting on the page ground -- it is sitting on a wash of itself. A value
# measured only against the page can still fail inside the chip, and three amber
# candidates did exactly that on 2026-08-05. Measure the chip.
# THE TOKEN IS `accent`, NOT `accent-1`. There is no `-1` anywhere in the
# canonical palette -- the four are `accent`, `accent-deep`, `accent-2` and
# `accent-soft`. `accent-1` is the natural thing to type once `accent-2` exists,
# it validates as a legal token NAME, and it resolves to nothing: reported once
# per build and painted in the body colour.
# ADDING A ROW RETROACTIVELY CLAIMS EVERY `{.name}` ALREADY WRITTEN
# An unknown marker is NOT an error: `on_page_markdown` hands it back untouched on
# purpose, because `{ .md-button }` is somebody else's attr_list syntax and eating
# it would be worse. So an author who invents a marker gets valid-looking
# markdown, plain body text, and one line in a build report.
# THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS, AND BOTH EDGES HAVE NOW DRAWN BLOOD. Before 2026-08-09,
# `uritp-docs` carried six `{.calc}`, five `{.button}` and one `{.portal}` that
# had never rendered -- reported every build, seen by nobody, which is the same
# shape as the `danger` callout that lost its red on 08-05. And in the other
# direction, `field` is a plausible attr_list class as well as a marker: nothing
# in the fleet uses it as one today (checked), but a future `{ .field }` meant as
# an HTML attribute will now render as a chip.
# `.value` WAS PROPOSED AND REFUSED (2026-08-09, Fiona) -- a marker for one entry
# ON a value list. Production MAWster already has a VALUES table with VALUES.tsv
# as its catalog, so every value is already a row in a file that renders. The
# distinction that decides the next one too: `.vl` is a THING OTHER OBJECTS POINT
# AT, so marking it records an edge; a value is a ROW IN A TABLE, and the answer
# to "show me all of them" is that table, not a report.
marker
column7: tooltip

column1: tbc
column7: Not yet verified against a source. Do not rely on this without checking.

column1: verify
column7: Recorded once and never re-checked. Measure it before you build to it.

column1: gap
column7: This fact should exist and does not. The absence is known, not overlooked.

column1: conf
column7: Double-checked against the real thing. Trust it.

column1: est
column7: Approximate. Close enough to plan with, not close enough to cut to.

column1: was
column7: The old VALUE, kept so paperwork quoting it can still be matched up. For an old NAME, use alias.

column1: term
column7: House terminology. Where it is also a link there is a page defining it.

column1: hi
column7: Flagged as worth your attention. This says nothing about whether the value is correct -- if you want that, the confidence markers are the ones that mean it.

column1: button
column7: A button on a FileMaker layout. The marked text is what the button SAYS, so it can be found by reading the label the way a user would.

column1: field
column7: A field placed on a layout. Names the object the user types into, not the underlying schema field -- for that, look the table up.

column1: portal
column7: A portal on a layout. Marks WHERE related records are shown; the relationship feeding it is a separate mark, and usually a rel link.

column1: layout
column7: A layout. Prefer the link form where the layout has a page, so the report records which layouts a workflow actually touches.

column1: calc
column7: A calculated value. NOTHING in FileMaker lists every calc in a file, so this marker is the only register there is. The link form takes a heading anchor: @calc:table-x#calc-name.

column1: rel
column7: A relationship between tables. The Graph shows it; nothing lists it as text. Prefer the link form so the report records the EDGE and not just the mention.

column1: script
column7: A script. Link it and the report becomes a call graph rather than a list of names.

column1: trigger
column7: A script trigger. Nothing in FileMaker enumerates these, and they are the objects most likely to be forgotten -- if it fires, mark it.

column1: global
column7: A global field or a $$variable. Scattered across a solution by nature; this is the only place they can be counted.

column1: vl
column7: A value list. Manage > Value Lists does enumerate these, so this marker is not the register -- it is here to record WHO USES IT, which is the part FileMaker cannot show you.

column1: alias
column7: A RETIRED NAME. Point it at the live one so paperwork quoting the old name still lands: [fkCal](@alias:table-x#calc-fkCalendar). For an old VALUE rather than an old name, use was.
